scientific_plan_amendments.reason: Reduces resource use (paid inference volume) and researcher degrees of freedom by introducing a small, cheap F/G screening stage ahead of the expensive full 136-effect two-model R_F reliability/calibration run. This amendment is NOT based on any observed DeepSeek/Gemma scientific performance difference -- none had been observed at the time of this amendment.

decision_rule.both_eligible: score both candidates with the already-frozen f_screen.py primary metric; existing tie-break order applies unchanged

paired_complete_case_ates.estimand: mean within-profile contrast (F reuses the same profile under control and treatment by design)
paired_complete_case_ates.minimum_n_rationale: under the 0.005 candidate-level gate, at most 30 invalid requests exist among 6,000; even maximally concentrated in one 250-profile effect this leaves >=220 paired-complete profiles -- reported transparently, not gated further
paired_complete_case_ates.rule: include profile i in an effect's ATE only if BOTH its control and treatment responses are valid; z_e,m = mean_i(Y_T - Y_C) over paired-complete profiles only
paired_complete_case_ates.unpaired_arm_means_rule_rejected: explicitly rejected when missingness differs between arms -- superseded by this paired-complete-case rule

scientific_plan_amendments.reason: The prior audit found no already-implemented, deterministic rule for reconciling missing/malformed/schema-invalid F-screen responses into the study-equal RMSE primary metric. This amendment freezes that rule BEFORE any DeepSeek/Gemma F-screen scientific results have been observed or retrieved. No candidate scientific performance was consulted in writing this rule.

atp1_atp2_overlap.scoring_implication: primary metric uses equal ITEM weighting (not equal-study weighting) for exactly this reason

atp_sample.eligibility_convention: reproduces datasets/atp{1,2}/evaluate.py's own dropna-after-RESPONSE_MAP convention exactly -- 'Not sure' and 'Refused/Web blank' excluded from human eligibility AND from model response support, not invented

external_g_prompt_path.does_not_alter: build_g_prompt_render (the frozen production target-G path) -- proven byte-for-byte unchanged by golden-hash regression tests (test_target_g_prompt_render_byte_identical_after_addition)

invalid_missing_handling.audit_finding: no G-specific numeric invalid-rate threshold exists anywhere in this repository; the F-screen 0.005 gate (ate.f_screen_validation.INVALID_RATE_GATE / ate.r_f_decision) is scoped to R/F production selection and is NOT auto-borrowed here
invalid_missing_handling.reason_not_reused: gate_decision embeds F's 0.005 numeric threshold (out of scope, not invented for G); paired_complete_case_effect assumes control/treatment pairing, which ATP has no equivalent of
invalid_missing_handling.rule: fail-closed, no invented threshold: a model/item is CLEAN only at exactly zero invalid responses; any nonzero invalid rate on any item blocks automatic G* selection for that model and requires an explicit, separate, contemporaneous methodological decision before that candidate's g_atp_loss is treated as final

primary_metric.formula: for each item, map ordered substantive response categories to equally spaced positions on [0,1] (fresh construction, NOT the source's own inconsistent 0-4/1-4 RESPONSE_MAP integers); W1_pp = 100 * wasserstein_distance(human_positions, model_positions); g_atp_loss = (W1_pp_ATP1 + W1_pp_ATP2) / 2
primary_metric.name: g_atp_loss
primary_metric.weighting: equal ITEM weight, not equal-study weight, because ATP1/ATP2 are not independent studies

decision.motivated_by: the request-identity/provenance overlap alone -- explicitly NOT by any observed R1 performance, since none had been generated

scientific_plan_amendments.equivalence_audit: scripts/prepare_f_reliability_r1_manifest.py + inline audit (not a committed script) confirmed, row-matched on (study_id, profile_id, condition_id, outcome_id): response_schema, engine_config_hash, prompt_protocol_id, prompt_compiler_version, required_fields, and response_key_map are 100% identical between the old and new manifests; only seed, custom_id, and request_stage differ (by construction, on every row); prompt_hash (rendered wording) coincidence rate between the two draws matches the pre-existing baseline rate already observed between the old manifest's replicate_id 1 and 2 (~2-3%), confirming this is normal variant-cycling behavior, not an anomaly introduced by the new draw identities

overlap_finding.mechanism: custom_id = hash(model|request_key); request_key embeds study_id/profile_id/condition_id/outcome_id/replicate_id only -- it has no notion of which pipeline stage requested it, so an identical (profile, effect, condition, replicate_id) tuple submitted twice under different stages hashes to the identical custom_id
overlap_finding.overlap_exactly_equals: the full set of Gemma f_model_screen custom_ids (replicate_id=1, first deterministic 250 profiles/effect x 12 effects x 2 conditions)

r1_design_unchanged.scale: 12 x 500 x 2 x 2 = 24,000, identical in shape to the original R1 design -- only the draw-identity labels changed

r1_draw_identity.derivation: replicate_id is a free integer input to the already-frozen deterministic machinery (inference.prompts.f_variant_assignment / stable_hash; inference.request_logging.seed_from_request_key) -- 3 and 4 are the next integers in the same formula already used for replicate_id 1 and 2, not a new convention; ate.r_f_decision.stage_r2_decision's four-draw (draw1..draw4) design already anticipated needing up to 4 independent draw identities
r1_draw_identity.replaces: replicate_ids 1 and 2 from the original (never-submitted) two-candidate f_reliability_pilot manifest, which remains on disk unmodified as a historical artifact
r1_draw_identity.verified_zero_overlap: 0 custom_id overlap and 0 seed overlap between the new 24,000-request R1 manifest and: F-model-screen (both candidates), G-model-screen (both candidates), the old f_reliability_pilot manifest (both candidates, never submitted), and the global submitted/successful id ledger

scientific_plan_amendments.r1_r2_plumbing_changes: none required -- ate.r_f_decision.stage_r1_decision/stage_r2_decision already accept two/four arbitrary per-effect z_pp DataFrames and internally relabel them replicate_1..replicate_4 for pairwise comparison, independent of whatever replicate_id value the source manifest used
scientific_plan_amendments.raw_output_scoring_glue: ate/f_reliability_validation.py (score_f_reliability_r1_from_raw), built and synthetic-tested (12 tests, tests/ate/test_f_reliability_validation.py) before any R1 inference -- reconciles, fully JSON-schema-validates, computes per-replicate paired-complete-case ATEs, and calls the unmodified ate.r_f_decision.stage_r1_decision; no coercion, clipping, imputation, or automatic retries
scientific_plan_amendments.reason: F* (google/gemma-4-31B-it) was selected mechanically under the frozen v4 F mini-screen (see f_screen_scoring_result.json, commit 6a25d3b73bd278c4134cb88a067cfe2805b80f5b). Auditing the pre-existing two-candidate f_reliability_pilot manifest before R1 submission found that 6,000 of Gemma's 24,000 R1 request custom_ids are byte-identical to already-submitted, already-retrieved-and-scored F-model-screen requests (same request_key -> same deterministic custom_id/seed, because both manifests draw the same 250-profile deterministic subset via the same nested_profile_subsets() function at replicate_id=1). This amendment freezes how R1 treats that overlap BEFORE any R1 scientific output was generated or observed.

operational_partitioning.rule: deterministic_profile_order() (the same function already used for nested N=50/100/250/500 selection) assigns each (study, profile) a stable position; partition = position % 4. Every partition therefore covers all 12 effects, both conditions, both replicates, exactly 125 profiles/effect -- verified, not assumed.

scientific_plan_amendments.reason: Historical R1 (batch e8674576-ba88-4385-9fe3-7ca5e2200d00, replicate_id 3/4, commit 96577ed27904c117f493ecf8204c1da744f18379) formally FAILED the frozen invalid-response-rate gate (0.4527, vs. threshold 0.005). A root-cause audit (offline, no new inference, no target inspection) found this was not stochastic treatment-effect instability but a provider-side structured-output serving-backend inconsistency: every invalid response (10,864/24,000) carried Together/vLLM system_fingerprint "vllm-0.21.0-8326ea74" (100% invalid within that subset) while every valid response (13,136/24,000) carried no fingerprint (0% invalid); F-screen (6,000 requests) and G-screen (1,226 requests) never touched the faulty backend and had 0% invalid. This amendment is a prospective engineering/format remediation, NOT a reaction to observed treatment-effect performance -- no R1 ATE/effect/ correlation/sign-agreement statistic informed this decision, and none may be inspected again until the complete replacement R1 dataset is retrieved.

remediation.golden_hash_regression: tests/inference/test_f_response_format_v2.py proves v1-default output is unaffected and that v1/v2 differ only in the closing instruction, all other model-visible content byte-identical
remediation.mechanism: inference/prompts.py build_f_prompt_render_from_items gains an opt-in response_format_instruction_version parameter ("v1" default, byte-identical to all prior behavior for every existing caller; "v2" for this amendment only). v2 replaces ONLY the closing instruction sentence with an explicit JSON-only / no-markdown / the real key name / "do not use the item's own letter label as a JSON key" instruction, plus a plain-text schema copy mechanically derived from the same item_json_schema() already sent via response_format (zero drift possible). No profile, stimulus, outcome wording, item label, response anchor, model, temperature, top_p, reasoning configuration, max_tokens, or schema field changed.

replacement_r1_design.note_one_benign_seed_collision: 1 of 24,000 seeds coincidentally matches one historical-R1 seed by 31-bit hash-reduction collision between two UNRELATED request_keys (different study/profile/effect/condition/replicate) -- confirmed not a duplicated request identity; custom_id overlap is exactly 0 everywhere

root_cause.contributing_factor: pre-existing, frozen archived-outcome wording embeds a letter item label (e.g. 'A. Frustrated') alongside a closing instruction that ambiguously said 'one integer value per item label'; identical text was present, harmless, in F-screen (0% invalid) -- necessary to explain WHY a non-enforced response said 'A', not sufficient to explain the rate difference
root_cause.decisive_evidence: system_fingerprint perfectly predicts validity (100% invalid on vllm-0.21.0-8326ea74, 0% invalid on the unlabeled/primary path); request_format_format (response_format/json_schema/strict/model/temperature/top_p/max_tokens/chat_template_kwargs) verified byte-identical (SHA256) between F-screen and R1
root_cause.ordinary_r2_infeasibility: mathematically proven, not assumed: reusing R1's draws 3/4 (10,864/24,000 invalid) as half of an R2 comparison yields a pooled invalid rate >= 10,864/48,000 = 22.63% even if the two new draws were 0% invalid -- vastly exceeding the frozen 0.005 gate regardless of new-draw quality

scientific_plan_amendments.new_operational_plan: part1 -> serving-validity check ONLY -> if invalid_rate<=0.005: parts 2, 3, 4 become eligible for submission in any order or concurrently (fan-out); if invalid_rate>0.005: STOP, parts 2/3/4 permanently blocked for this replacement attempt, no retries
scientific_plan_amendments.old_operational_plan: part1 -> validity check -> part2 -> validity check -> part3 -> validity check -> part4 (strictly sequential)
scientific_plan_amendments.reason: Purely operational change to replacement-R1 provider submission scheduling, made BEFORE any replacement-R1 output was observed. Elapsed time is currently more costly to the user than the residual Parts 2-4 inference cost; retains exactly one 6,000-request prospective serving-qualification partition (part1) to detect recurrence of the known structured-output failure before exposing the remaining 18,000 requests, but no longer requires parts 2, 3, and 4 to gate on each other sequentially.

state_machine.STATE_0: nothing recorded; only part1 may be submitted
state_machine.STATE_1: part1 submitted, not yet retrieved/scored; parts 2/3/4 still forbidden
state_machine.STATE_2_FAIL: part1 recorded FAIL; parts 2/3/4 permanently blocked for this replacement attempt
state_machine.STATE_2_PASS: part1 recorded PASS (reused 0.005 threshold); parts 2/3/4 all independently eligible, no inter-dependency among them

production_config_prepared_not_authorize.note: These two config values are set to match the frozen R_F=1 so that any future production run uses the correct, already-decided draw count. Setting them is plumbing only -- it does not submit, queue, or authorize any calibration or target inference; f_reliability.py's f_protocol_config() only ever reads these values, never triggers a submission as a side effect of being set.

scientific_plan_amendments.reason: All four operational partitions (part1-part4) of the replacement R1 (google/gemma-4-31B-it, replicate_ids 5/6, format-only v2 remediation) completed and were retrieved. Reconciled against the single canonical 24,000-request manifest and scored via the unmodified, already-frozen pipeline (ate/f_reliability_validation.score_f_reliability_r1_from_raw -> ate/r_f_decision.stage_r1_decision). All three frozen R1 gates passed. This entry records that outcome and the resulting R_F=1 freeze; it is NOT a pre-results rule change like the amendments above it -- the rule itself (thresholds, scorer, decision procedure) is completely unchanged.
